tiers.label: Foundations
tiers.description: For the reader starting from scratch: the on-ramp before any real course.

tiers.label: Core
tiers.description: For the new student: the first course in each broad area, taken by everyone.

tiers.label: Advanced core
tiers.description: For the reader with the core done: second courses, the shared toolkit of every mathematician.

tiers.label: Specialization
tiers.description: For the reader committed to an area: the entry books of each research track.

tiers.label: Frontier
tiers.description: For the specialist: books whose goal is current research.

nodes.title: Abelian Varieties
nodes.description: complex tori, polarizations, theta functions, isogenies, the dual abelian variety, and abelian varieties over general fields. Two Parts: (I) complex-analytic, complex tori, the Appell–Humbert theorem, the Riemann relations, theta functions, the dual torus and isogenies, endomorphism algebras and CM; (II) algebraic over arbitrary fields (full scheme-theoretic), rigidity, the theorem of the cube, Tate modules, the dual abelian variety and the Weil pairing, the Rosati involution and Albert's classification, Jacobians, and abelian varieties over finite fields (Frobenius, Weil conjectures, Honda–Tate). Prereqs Algebraic Geometry, Complex Analysis, Commutative Algebra, Homological Algebra; strongly recommended Elliptic Curves (the g=1 model). Keystone of the arithmetic-geometry tower, between Elliptic Curves and Shimura Varieties.

nodes.title: Algebraic Geometry
nodes.description: Presheaves and sheaves, stalks, sheafification, direct and inverse image; affine schemes, Spec and the structure sheaf, gluing, the functor of points; morphisms (separated, proper, finite, flat, smooth), fibre products, Proj; group schemes and Hopf algebras; quasi-coherent and coherent sheaves, projective morphisms, divisors and the Picard group, differentials; sheaf cohomology, Čech, the cohomology of projective space, Serre finiteness and vanishing, Ext and Serre duality; curves and surfaces: Riemann-Roch, the Hodge index theorem, Noether's formula, adjunction, blow-ups, the 27 lines on a cubic surface.

nodes.title: Algebraic K-Theory
nodes.description: projective modules and Pic, K_0 (with H_0 and Morita equivalence), K_1 (Whitehead group), K_2 (Steinberg group, universal central extensions), Milnor K-theory and Matsumoto's theorem, Quillen's higher K-theory (BGL^+, the Q-construction, +=Q), the fundamental theorems (resolution, dévissage, localization, Bass), K-theory of schemes, and the computations (K_*(F_q), Dedekind domains, K_*(O_K) and Borel's theorem). The non-periodic side of the K-theory family. **Owns Quillen's Theorem A/B and the plus construction natively**, Algebraic Topology has none of that machinery and no consumer for it; it supplies only BG, pi_n, fibration sequences and the Serre spectral sequence. Cites Higher Category Theory for the nerve and geometric realization. 1–3 drafted-unaudited, Ch. 5 blocked on the nerve).

nodes.title: Algebraic Number Theory
nodes.description: rings of integers, ideals, integral bases, norms, traces, splitting of primes, ideal class group, Dirichlet's unit theorem, Kronecker-Weber theorem.

nodes.title: Algebraic Topology
nodes.description: fundamental group, covering spaces, singular homology, CW complexes, cohomology rings, Poincaré duality.

nodes.title: Multivariable Calculus
nodes.description: Differentiation in R^n, the inverse and implicit function theorems, multiple integrals and change of variables, smooth partitions of unity on R^n (partition-of-unity stratum A), and the classical vector calculus through Green/Stokes/divergence in 2-3 dimensions.

nodes.title: Category Theory
nodes.description: the working categorical language (strict 1-category theory), in eight chapters: categories/functors/natural transformations, the Yoneda lemma and representability, universal properties with limits and colimits, adjunctions (including the adjoint functor theorems), monads and their algebras, **Kan extensions** as the core-theory capstone ("all concepts are Kan extensions"), then a structured-categories coda, **monoidal categories** (Mac Lane coherence, symmetric/closed) and **enriched and (strict) 2-categories**, that ends by pointing across the coherence seam to the weak/homotopical sequel Higher Category Theory. Standing cast of example categories in place of one running example; arc credited to Riehl's *Category Theory in Context*. **Abelian categories are deliberately ceded to Homological Algebra**. A subfiles sub-book compiled into the *Algebra* mega-book (the "Category Theory" Part) that also compiles standalone with the full EYNTKA skeleton, guarded via ifstandalonesubfile.

nodes.title: Class Field Theory
nodes.description: local fields, places, ray class groups, idele group, Hasse principle.

nodes.title: Classical Algebraic Geometry
nodes.description: algebraic sets, varieties, normalization, dimension, blow-ups.

nodes.title: Commutative Algebra
nodes.description: integral extensions, localization, completion, Hilbert's basis theorem.

nodes.title: Complex Analysis
nodes.description: Cauchy–Riemann, analytic continuation, residue theorem, elliptic functions, Riemann surfaces.

nodes.title: Complex Analytic Geometry
nodes.description: the analytic geometry of complex manifolds and complex analytic sets, in four Parts: (I) *foundations*, holomorphic functions of several variables, the local ring of convergent power series with Weierstrass division, complex manifolds and the partial/barpartial splitting, holomorphic bundles and divisors; (II) *pseudoconvexity and the barpartial-equation*, plurisubharmonicity, the three-way equivalence with holomorphic convexity and Levi pseudoconvexity, Hörmander's L^2 estimates, and Newlander–Nirenberg; (III) *coherence, Stein theory and analytic sets*, Oka and Cartan coherence, Theorems A and B, the Cousin problems and the Oka principle, the local structure of analytic sets, Remmert–Stein and Chow, and currents/Lelong through the fundamental class of a singular projective variety; (IV) *positivity and the analytic–algebraic bridge*, Chern curvature and positivity, Kodaira–Nakano vanishing, the Kodaira embedding theorem, and Kodaira–Spencer deformations. The series' supplier of the fundamental class Intersection Theory Ch. 6 §2 needs, of the complex-manifold and line-bundle layer Abelian Varieties currently miscites to Complex Analysis, and of the Kodaira embedding theorem Algebraic Geometry cites with no owner. Carved so that Hodge Theory keeps compact **Kähler** geometry, metrics, the Kähler identities, harmonic theory, the Hodge decomposition, and everything structural above it; NateComplexGeometry was considered and rejected as a name for exactly that reason. **Part I is a staged migration of Hodge Theory Ch. 1, Ch. 2 §2 and App. A, approved but not yet executed** (BOOK.md §11).

nodes.title: Core Algebra
nodes.description: groups, rings, modules, fields.

nodes.title: Core Probability
nodes.description: the measure-free treatment (measure theory built inline, not assumed): distributions, expected value, variance, law of large numbers, Erdős-Rényi graphs, exponential/concentration inequalities, Gaussian distribution, finite Markov chains. The accessible entry point; the measure-theoretic flagship is *Probability*.

nodes.title: Core Representation Theory
nodes.description: Maschke's theorem, Schur's lemma, Wedderburn-Artin theorem, character theory, induced representations, Frobenius reciprocity, quiver theory.

nodes.title: C*-Algebras and K-Theory
nodes.description: C*-algebras, Gelfand–Naimark duality, states and the GNS construction, representations, and the K-theory of C*-algebras (K_0/K_1, six-term exact sequence, Bott, the Toeplitz index map).

nodes.title: Differential Topology
nodes.description: the smooth-manifold substrate and its topological payoffs: smooth manifolds and maps, transversality and intersection theory, Sard's and Whitney's theorems, vector fields and flows, bundles, differential forms and integration, and de Rham cohomology. The genuinely metric/curvature material lives downstream in Riemannian Geometry; Lie theory in Lie Groups.

nodes.title: Elementary Analysis
nodes.description: the single-variable spine: construction and completeness of R, sequences and series, limits and continuity, differentiation, and the Riemann integral.

nodes.title: Elliptic Curves
nodes.description: Weierstrass equations, group law, isogenies, Weil pairing, Mordell–Weil theorem, Hasse's theorem, Galois representations, CM theory, modular forms, modularity, BSD conjecture.

nodes.title: Étale Cohomology
nodes.description: the étale site and étale cohomology of schemes. Four Parts (14 chapters): (I) *the étale topology*, étale morphisms and Henselian local rings, the étale fundamental group pi_1^ét (finite étale covers, Galois categories, Riemann existence, owned here, the series' home of the topic), the étale site and its sheaves; (II) *étale cohomology*, cohomology and the cohomology of a point (= Galois cohomology), Kummer/Artin–Schreier/G_m, the cohomology of curves, constructible sheaves and finiteness; (III) *the Brauer group and the fundamental theorems*, the cohomological Brauer group Br(X)=H^2_ét(X,G_m) (Azumaya, **Gabber proved**), base change / Künneth / comparison, purity / cycle class / Poincaré duality; (IV) *ell-adic cohomology and the Weil conjectures*, ell-adic sheaves, the Lefschetz trace formula + rationality + functional equation, Lefschetz pencils and vanishing cycles, and **Deligne's proof of the Riemann Hypothesis in full** (Weil I). The series' bridge from scheme theory to arithmetic geometry, the upstream home of the geometric Brauer group, and the home of the étale fundamental group. Prereqs Algebraic Geometry, Commutative Algebra, Homological Algebra, Group and Galois Cohomology; **co-requisite Moduli, Deformation Theory, and Stacks** (cites its descent/sites + gerbe interpretation of H^2; supplies back the Gabber proof + higher-dimensional Brauer computations that book defers). Feeds Moduli, Deformation Theory, and Stacks, Hodge Theory (cycle class map / comparison), Abelian Varieties.

nodes.title: Functional Analysis
nodes.description: Banach spaces, Hilbert spaces, Hahn–Banach theorem, open mapping theorem, spectral theory of bounded operators.

nodes.title: Group and Galois Cohomology
nodes.description: the series' cohomological source-book, in three arcs: **group cohomology** (discrete + finite: derived functors, the bar resolution, low-degree interpretations and extensions, homology and coinvariants, Tate cohomology and cup products), **structure theory** (cohomological dimension, pro-p groups and Golod–Shafarevich, the Brauer group), and **Galois cohomology of fields** (the profinite refinement, local and global Tate duality, the Poitou–Tate sequence, class formations and reciprocity, descent and non-abelian cohomology, Selmer/Ш). Feeds Class Field Theory, Elliptic Curves, Local Langlands for GL₂(F), Moduli, Deformation Theory, and Stacks, Étale Cohomology.

nodes.title: Algebraic Groups and Representations
nodes.description: linear algebraic groups, root systems, Dynkin classification, highest-weight theory, Weyl character formula, Borel–Weil–Bott.

nodes.title: Harmonic Analysis
nodes.description: Fourier transform, convolution, distribution theory, Sobolev spaces, topological groups, Haar measure, Pontryagin duality.

nodes.title: Hodge Theory
nodes.description: compact Kähler geometry, Hodge decomposition, polarized Hodge structures, Lefschetz theorems, variations of Hodge structure, period maps and Mumford–Tate domains, mixed Hodge structures, algebraic cycles.

nodes.title: Homological Algebra
nodes.description: abelian categories, localization of categories and the derived category, derived functors (Ext/Tor), group cohomology, homological dimension, and spectral sequences. **Supply caveat:** the *triangulated*-category material is sec:derivAndTriangCat, a starred bonus section its own BOOK.md §4 marks pre-framework and unassessed (a live ref:HERE placeholder, a note-to-self parenthetical, a triangulatedd typo). Higher Category Theory Ch. 5 is contracted to cite it for the 1-categorical original of a stable ∞-category, so that chapter should not be drafted before Ch. 3 is assessed. See BACKLOG.

nodes.title: Intersection Theory
nodes.description: Algebraic cycles and rational equivalence; Chow groups, proper pushforward and flat pullback; divisors and the first Chern class as an operator; cones, Segre classes, Chern classes and the splitting principle; deformation to the normal cone, specialization of cycles and the Gysin map of a regular embedding; the intersection product, the Chow ring, self-intersection and excess, Bezout and the agreement with the classical surface pairing; cycle class maps and adequate equivalence relations (coming soon); Grothendieck-Riemann-Roch (coming soon); Schubert calculus and degeneracy loci (coming soon).

nodes.title: Vector Bundles and K-Theory
nodes.description: topological K-theory in nine chapters: vector bundles and their classification by BO/BU; K^0, K^1, the negative and relative groups, and the ring structure; **Bott periodicity, proved here** by the clutching/linearization route, with K* as a 2-periodic generalized cohomology theory; the **Chern character** and the integrality it forces; **Adams operations** and what only they reach, Hopf invariant one, Hurwitz's theorem on real division algebras, parallelizable spheres; **real K-theory** and eight-fold periodicity via Clifford modules and Atiyah–Bott–Shapiro, with the vector-fields-on-spheres bound; the **K-theoretic Thom class and Gysin pushforward**, the Todd genus, and the statement of Atiyah–Singer; **Fredholm operators** and Atiyah–Jänich; and **equivariant K-theory** through K_G(pt)=R(G) and the Atiyah–Segal completion theorem. Purely topological. Prereqs Algebraic Topology, Differential Topology; coreqs Algebraic K-Theory, C*-Algebras and K-Theory; feeds the planned Spin Geometry and Index Theory (Chern character, Thom class) and NateStableHomotopy (KU as the motivating generalized theory).

nodes.title: Local Langlands for GL₂(F)
nodes.description: 5 §§3-5 are unwritten placeholders, including the converse theorem that the titular theorem's proof invokes; Chs. 3/4/7 are in sketch register; no exercises and no closing chapter. See langlands-gl2/BOOK.md §11.

nodes.title: Lie Groups
nodes.description: the analytic / differential-geometric half of Lie theory, complementary to the algebraic-groups treatment in Algebraic Groups and Representations. Four Parts: (I) Lie groups and their Lie algebras, matrix groups and the classical groups, the exponential map, left-invariant vector fields, the closed-subgroup theorem, the Lie group–Lie algebra correspondence, BCH, homogeneous spaces and covering groups; (II) structure of Lie algebras, solvable/nilpotent (Engel, Lie), the Cartan criteria, Weyl complete reducibility, Levi, the root space decomposition, root systems, and the Cartan–Killing classification; (III) compact Lie groups and their representations, invariant integration, the Peter–Weyl theorem, maximal tori and the Weyl integration formula, the Weyl character and dimension formulas; (IV) real forms and symmetric spaces, complexification, the Cartan decomposition, the Iwasawa decomposition KAN, and Riemannian symmetric spaces bridging to Riemannian Geometry. Running example SU(2). Prereqs Differential Topology, Core Algebra, Core Representation Theory, Topology, NateRealAnalysis/Functional Analysis; cites Harmonic Analysis for Haar measure.

nodes.title: Linear Algebra
nodes.description: Finite-dimensional linear algebra over R and C: systems and elimination, vector spaces and the four fundamental subspaces, determinants as volume, eigenvalues; then inner products, orthogonality, least squares and the spectral theorem; quadratic forms and Sylvester's law of inertia, the SVD and polar decomposition, generalized eigenspaces and the real Jordan form; closing with conditioning, eigenvalue perturbation, iterative computation, and Perron-Frobenius.

nodes.title: Linear Elliptic and Parabolic PDE
nodes.description: the graduate linear-PDE spine: weak formulations and Lax–Milgram, existence by variational methods, the two regularity theories (Schauder and L^p), maximum principles, Green's functions, spectral theory of elliptic operators, and the heat equation with semigroups; elliptic systems on domains. Cites the analysis foundations for Sobolev/distributions/singular integrals (does not re-derive them). Prereqs Functional Analysis, Measure Theory, Harmonic Analysis, Multivariable Calculus.

nodes.title: Logic
nodes.description: first-order language, propositional language, soundness, completeness, compactness, computability, Turing machines, Gödel's incompleteness theorem.

nodes.title: Measure Theory
nodes.description: sigma-algebras, outer measure, Borel/Lebesgue measures, product measure, signed and complex measures, Lebesgue-Radon-Nikodym theorem.

nodes.title: Analysis on Metric and Function Spaces
nodes.description: Metric spaces and completeness, the Banach contraction principle, compactness (sequential and totally bounded), uniform convergence, and the function-space theorems: Stone-Weierstrass, Arzela-Ascoli, and Baire category.

nodes.title: Moduli, Deformation Theory, and Stacks
nodes.description: Moduli theory in three movements: representability and the construction toolkit (Hilbert/Quot schemes, geometric invariant theory); deformation theory (first-order deformations, obstructions, the cotangent complex, Schlessinger's criteria); and algebraic stacks (descent and sites, fibered categories, Deligne-Mumford and Artin stacks, gerbes and the Brauer group). Closes with the moduli of curves.

nodes.title: Nonlinear Wave and Dispersive PDE
nodes.description: linear wave (d'Alembert, energy method) as the foundation, then nonlinear wave equations (Klainerman–Sobolev, null conditions, global existence) and dispersive methods (Littlewood–Paley, Strichartz). The analytic engine of general relativity (the Einstein equations are a nonlinear wave system). The linear elliptic/parabolic core moved to Linear Elliptic and Parabolic PDE. Prereqs Functional Analysis, Ordinary Differential Equations (ODE), Multivariable Calculus, Harmonic Analysis.

nodes.title: Ordinary Differential Equations (ODE)
nodes.description: Picard-Lindelöf theorem, linear systems, matrix exponentials, Lyapunov stability, boundary value problems, Sturm-Liouville theory, Green's functions.

nodes.title: Preliminaries
nodes.description: series-wide foundation: logic, naive set theory, proof techniques, relations and orders, functions, cardinality, elementary number theory, first exposure to categories.

nodes.title: Probability
nodes.description: Measure-theoretic probability: probability spaces, random variables and independence, modes of convergence, laws of large numbers, characteristic functions and the central limit theorem, conditional expectation via Radon–Nikodym, and discrete-time martingales. Ends before continuous-time processes.

nodes.title: Riemannian Geometry
nodes.description: a two-Part backbone. Part I (metric Riemannian geometry): metrics of arbitrary signature, the Levi-Civita connection, geodesics and the exponential map, the curvature tensor, Jacobi fields, comparison theorems (Hopf–Rinow, Bonnet–Myers, Cartan–Hadamard, Rauch), submanifold geometry, curvature and topology, homogeneous and symmetric spaces. Part II (analysis and curvature on manifolds): connections and curvature on vector bundles, Chern–Weil theory, the Hodge–de Rham theorem, the Bochner technique. Pseudo-Riemannian threaded throughout for downstream GR. Prereqs Differential Topology, NateRealAnalysis, Linear Elliptic and Parabolic PDE. Part II is a pre-cut split seam. Feeds Hodge Theory (which imports Part II), geometric analysis, GR, and spin/index theory.

nodes.title: Shimura Varieties
nodes.description: the arithmetic-geometry capstone above Abelian Varieties and the geometric gateway to the Langlands program, following Deligne's axiomatic Hodge-theoretic route (Milne/Deligne). Four Parts, twelve chapters: (I) *from modular curves to symmetric domains*, the modular curve as prototype, Hermitian symmetric domains and their three faces, and Hodge structures as representations of the Deligne torus S=Res_C/RG_m; (II) *Shimura data and Shimura varieties*, the axioms SV1-SV3 on a pair (G,X), the reflex field, the double-coset variety G(Q)backslash Xtimes G(A_f)/K with its component structure and Hecke action, and Baily-Borel algebraicity; (III) *canonical models and PEL moduli*, CM/special points and the reciprocity law, existence and uniqueness of canonical models over the reflex field, the Siegel variety A_g and PEL-type moduli of abelian varieties; (IV) *toward automorphic forms and Langlands*, automorphic vector bundles and forms, and the cohomology of Shimura varieties carrying Galois representations (Eichler-Shimura prototype, Langlands-Kottwitz survey). Running examples: the modular curve (GL_2) and the Siegel variety (GSp_2g). Prereqs Abelian Varieties (CM, Albert, Tate modules), Elliptic Curves, Algebraic Groups and Representations, Class Field Theory; coreq Hodge Theory (Mumford-Tate/period domains). The legacy Serre-preliminaries stub (central simple algebras / Brauer group) was archived at bootstrap and cited out to Group and Galois Cohomology/Core Algebra.

nodes.title: Mathematical Statistics
nodes.description: Mathematical statistics on a measure-theoretic base: statistical models and the decision-theoretic frame, sufficiency and exponential families, point estimation (Cramér–Rao, UMVU, MLE, Bayes), hypothesis testing and confidence sets (Neyman–Pearson, likelihood ratio, duality), large-sample theory, and the Gaussian linear model.

nodes.title: Topology
nodes.description: separation axioms, product/quotient topology, metric spaces, connectedness, compactness, Urysohn lemma, fundamental group, topological groups.

nodes.title: Toric Geometry
nodes.description: the combinatoricsleftrightarrowgeometry dictionary: tori and character lattices; affine toric varieties (the four constructions and their equivalence); rational polyhedral cones, Gordan's lemma, and normal affine toric varieties; projective toric varieties and lattice polytopes; fans and abstract toric varieties; completeness, properness, and toric morphisms; the orbit–cone correspondence; toric Weil/Cartier divisors and the class group; the Cox homogeneous-coordinate construction (toric varieties as torus quotients); ample/nef cones and line bundles; sheaf cohomology of toric varieties and toric Riemann–Roch (lattice-point counting); toric resolution of singularities; capstone on reflexive polytopes, Fano toric varieties, and Batyrev mirror symmetry. **Two-register bridge:** the combinatorial spine (Parts I–IV) is developed over k=bar k (default C) and requires only *Classical Algebraic Geometry* + *Commutative Algebra*; scheme-theoretic material is threaded as marked "Scheme upgrade" asides, and the cohomology Part escalates to *Algebraic Geometry* as a recommended co-requisite. The book is thus both a gateway example-bed reachable before schemes and a payoff of scheme theory, the series' canonical toric example-bed.

clusters.label: Langlands programme
clusters.description: Toward the local Langlands correspondence for GL₂, representation theory and class field theory up through smooth representations and the GL₂ case.

clusters.label: Arithmetic geometry
clusters.description: The arithmetic of varieties, elliptic curves, abelian varieties, and Shimura varieties over number fields, resting on algebraic and arithmetic foundations.

clusters.label: Hodge theory & cycles
clusters.description: Complex and Kähler geometry toward Hodge theory, algebraic cycles, and the (integral) Hodge conjecture.

clusters.label: K-theory
clusters.description: The three flavours of K-theory, topological, algebraic, and operator (C*), and their shared homotopical/homological foundations.

clusters.label: Analysis → PDE
clusters.description: The analysis ladder, from elementary analysis through measure theory and functional analysis to ODE and PDE.
